scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: Dispute surge driven by incorrect bills requiring AI agent to auto-answer and fix root cause.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: AMI read data missing or delayed, causing estimation errors and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-ISSUE.statement: Field manual read process failures (route completion gaps) leading to estimates and billing errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced in August causing systematic mis-bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows disputed bills include both ESTIMATED (1240) and ACTUAL (1785) read types, with more disputes on actual reads. This indicates the dispute surge is not solely driven by estimation errors; issues also affect bills based on actual meter reads.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a gap in the field manual read process that can lead to estimation errors and billing disputes.
The tariff change log shows no recent tariff changes, indicating that tariff alterations are not contributing to the dispute surge.
The dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to over 1100 in August and 1260 in September, showing a clear increase starting in August.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

The observation shows dispute ticket response times are within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs SLA 3.0 days) for 2,440 tickets, indicating that response speed is not a limiting factor in the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows 320 accounts had estimated reads in the last billing cycle across 40 distinct routes, indicating a substantial number of estimation events that could contribute to billing disputes.

U-U1.question: Whether the billing import validation rule change actually caused the systematic mis-bills.
